missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

When the photometric characteristics of any lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, the lamp shall ensure any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5º (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit shall be permitted to be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
The tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
The ESA representative of its type shall have a measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V (12V system) or +37 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V (12V system) or +20 V (24V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.
The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device in case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be removed with the use of tool(s) in case of replaceable light source module(s).
The stop lamp shall emit red light.
The measured values shall not deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
The measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3.

extra.text: The ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
extra.test_case: Inspect the submitted lamp samples for a clear, indelible trade name/mark and type designation.

extra.text: In case the ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128 granted to this ESA, or provide a test report by a Technical Service stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
extra.test_case: Check documentation provides R37/R99/R128 approval number or Technical Service report of non-interchangeability.

extra.text: The representative ESA system(s) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7. of this Regulation for type approval to be granted.
extra.test_case: Review test report showing the lamp ESA meets all paragraph 6 requirements.

extra.text: In case the ESA is (part of) a light source and the documentation as specified in paragraph 3.2.10. is missing, approval of this ESA according to Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.
extra.test_case: Confirm paragraph 3.2.10 documentation is present before approval.

extra.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
extra.test_case: Verify mark location matches the place specified on the communication form.

extra.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect mark for circle with E and the approving country's number.

extra.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
extra.test_case: Inspect mark for "10R-" followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.

extra.text: The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
extra.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of the lamp per Annex 7 (ALSE method) and confirm a test report exists.

extra.text: The maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems, as given in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Check measured positive transient amplitudes do not exceed +75 V (12 V) / +150 V (24 V).

extra.text: When tested with the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be tested at 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band (Table 2a) and at a minimum of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band (Table 2b).
extra.test_case: Verify stripline test levels of 60 V/m (>90 % of band) and minimum 50 V/m over 20-400 MHz were applied.

extra.text: When tested with the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be tested at 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz band and 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band (Table 2a), and at a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz band and 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band (Table 2b).
extra.test_case: Verify ALSE test levels of 30/10 V/m (>90 % of band) and minimum 25/8 V/m were applied over 80-6,000 MHz.

extra.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be tested at 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz band and 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band (Table 2a), and at a minimum of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz band and 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band (Table 2b).
extra.test_case: Verify reverberation chamber test levels of 21/7 V/m (>90 % of band) and minimum 18/6 V/m were applied.

extra.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limits for the ESA shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
extra.test_case: Measure broadband emissions per Annex 7 from 30 to 75 MHz and verify all values are below the logarithmically decreasing 62 to 52 dBµV/m limit.

extra.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limits for the ESA shall be 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
extra.test_case: Measure broadband emissions per Annex 7 from 75 to 400 MHz and verify all values are below the logarithmically increasing 52 to 63 dBµV/m limit.

extra.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the broadband limit for the ESA remains constant at 63 dBµV/m.
extra.test_case: Measure broadband emissions per Annex 7 from 400 to 1,000 MHz and verify all values are below 63 dBµV/m.

extra.text: For the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the broadband radiated emissions of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
extra.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions per Annex 7 with 120 kHz bandwidth over 30-75 MHz and verify all values are below E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: For the frequency range 75-400 MHz, the broadband radiated emissions of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
extra.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions with 120 kHz bandwidth over 75-400 MHz and verify all values are below E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m.

extra.text: For the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the narrowband radiated emissions of the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.).
extra.test_case: Measure ESA narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 with 120 kHz bandwidth over 30-75 MHz and verify all values are below E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω artificial network (AN) as defined in Figure 1 shall be used.
extra.test_case: Check the ESA test set-up records show a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN per Figure 1 in the LV supply lines.

extra.text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the test measuring broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Review the test report to confirm the broadband radiated emission test was carried out to CISPR 25.

extra.text: For an ESA other than one involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the radiated broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Check the test set-up record shows the CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 ALSE arrangement (or permitted OATS alternative).

extra.text: The radiated broadband emission limits shall apply to the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz and verify all readings are below the paragraph 6.5 limits.

extra.text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 8, the measurement of radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Review the narrowband emission test report and confirm the test set-up and procedure follow CISPR 25.

extra.text: During the narrowband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Verify in the test report that the lamp functions were operated in normal mode with all functions at maximum load during measurement.

extra.text: The narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Confirm the test report shows an ALSE set-up per CISPR 25 clause 6.4 (or a CISPR 16-1-4 compliant OATS).

extra.text: The narrowband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Verify the measured narrowband emissions across 30-1,000 MHz are below the applicable limits.

extra.text: The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
extra.test_case: Confirm in the test report that the average detector was used for all narrowband readings.

extra.text: The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver, using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2.
extra.test_case: Check the instrument type and settings recorded in the test report against Tables 1 and 2.

extra.text: The ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the test methods (absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5, reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11) at the manufacturer's discretion only provided that these result in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered.
extra.test_case: Review the immunity test report and confirm that the selected method(s) together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps.

extra.text: For the immunity test of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation, the frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check that the test plan and report reference ISO 11452-1 for the frequency range and general conditions.

extra.text: During the immunity test of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation, the test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Verify in the test report that the test conditions (temperature, supply voltage, etc.) follow ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
extra.test_case: Confirm that during the test the lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) are energised and operating normally.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
extra.test_case: Inspect the test set-up photos and description against the Annex 9 arrangement.

extra.text: The frequency step size and dwell time for the ESA immunity test shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check the test report step size and dwell time against ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: For the absorber chamber test, the "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
extra.test_case: Check that the field calibration in the absorber chamber used the ISO 11452-2 substitution method.

extra.text: The absorber chamber test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
extra.test_case: Verify in the test report that the antenna polarization was vertical.

extra.text: The TEM cell test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with the method of maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM-cell chosen depending on the ESA to be tested.
extra.test_case: Check that the TEM cell test followed ISO 11452-3 and that the coupling orientation chosen is documented.

extra.text: The bulk current injection test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, using either the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or the BCI closed loop method with the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
extra.test_case: Verify the BCI method used and measure the probe distance: 150 mm for substitution or 900 mm for closed loop.

extra.text: The stripline test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
extra.test_case: Check that the stripline test set-up and procedure in the report follow ISO 11452-5.

extra.text: The reverberation chamber test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
extra.test_case: Check that the reverberation chamber test followed ISO 11452-11.

extra.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
extra.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emissions of the lamp per ISO 7637-2 on its supply lines and compare them with the limits of the Regulation.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.
extra.test_case: Place the unladen vehicle on a flat horizontal surface and measure the lamp height and orientation in that condition.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).
extra.test_case: Measure the left and right lamp positions from the median longitudinal plane using the exterior lamp form and confirm symmetry.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
extra.test_case: Compare the left and right lamps and confirm they are mirror-symmetrical externally.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
extra.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of each function on the left and right lamps and confirm both meet the same colour requirements.

extra.text: Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps shall not be reciprocally incorporated.
extra.test_case: Inspect the lamp design and confirm the stop lamp does not share a common illuminating surface with a direction indicator.

extra.text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
extra.test_case: Project the two apparent surfaces and confirm ≥60 % fill of the circumscribing quadrilateral or ≤75 mm gap.

extra.text: The maximum height above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
extra.test_case: Measure each function's highest and lowest apparent-surface points above the ground in the reference-axis direction.

extra.text: For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
extra.test_case: Measure the height of the H plane above the ground and use it to justify any reduced vertical visibility angle.

extra.text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
extra.test_case: Per Annex 4, check from Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m ahead of the vehicle that no part of the red apparent surface is directly visible.

extra.text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
extra.test_case: Operate the function and confirm all light sources of the interdependent lamp system switch ON and OFF together.

extra.text: The concealment of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be prohibited.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installation and confirm the rear lamp functions are not concealable.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
extra.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the reversing lamp and confirm it is within the white boundaries.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
extra.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the stop lamp and confirm it is within the red boundaries.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
extra.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the rear position lamp and confirm it is within the red boundaries.

extra.text: The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
extra.test_case: Verify the retro-reflector colour is red by colorimetric check per its device approval.

extra.text: The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Count the lamps of each function on the vehicle and compare against the individual specifications in paragraph 6.

extra.text: The rear lamp may be installed on movable components only provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
extra.test_case: If mounted on a movable component, verify compliance with paragraphs 5.18 to 5.20.

extra.text: Rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
extra.test_case: With the movable component in each fixed position, check position, geometric visibility, colour and photometry of the lamps.

extra.text: When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the lamps installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.
extra.test_case: With the movable component open, assess that the lamps do not cause undue discomfort (glare) to road users.

extra.text: When the lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Operate the movable component repeatedly and confirm the lamp returns to the manufacturer-specified position.

extra.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".
extra.test_case: With the movable component in each fixed open position, measure the hidden share of the apparent surface and confirm it does not exceed 50 per cent.

extra.text: With the exception of retro-reflectors, the rear position, stop and reversing lamps, even bearing an approval mark, are deemed not to be present when they cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
extra.test_case: Verify on the installed vehicle that each lamp function operates without anything other than fitting a light source and/or fuse.

extra.text: Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light sources, shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Perform a light-source replacement on the installed lamp using only vehicle-supplied tools; pass if correctly replaced without expert help.

extra.text: Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are allowed only provided that the intensity of all such lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
extra.test_case: Measure intensities of the R2/S2 lamps across the variation range and verify they vary together proportionally.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.
extra.test_case: Measure stop/position intensity ratio during transitions and verify the prescribed ratio is maintained.

extra.text: If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
extra.test_case: Photometrically measure the lamp with the obscuring parts in place; pass if prescribed values are still met.

extra.text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
extra.test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps together and verify the geometric visibility angles.

extra.text: A LED module of the lamp need not be replaceable only if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.
extra.test_case: Check the device approval communication sheet states the LED module is non-replaceable.

extra.text: In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.
extra.test_case: Verify R148 approval covering the lamp with logo.

extra.text: Lamps installed on the vehicle and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
extra.test_case: Inspect fitted light sources and confirm they carry approval for the categories stated in the lamp approval.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall be present on motor vehicles (mandatory).
extra.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle installation and confirm at least one reversing lamp is fitted.

extra.text: On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second device is optional.
extra.test_case: Count reversing lamps on the M1 vehicle; pass if one or two devices are fitted.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angles α and β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device.
extra.test_case: Verify the apparent surface is visible over 15° up, 5° down and 45° left and right.

extra.text: For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angles α and β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.
extra.test_case: Verify each lamp's apparent surface is visible over 15° up, 5° down, 45° outwards and 30° inwards.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp and confirm its reference axis points rearwards.

extra.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
extra.test_case: Check component approval; if failure indication is required, simulate failure and confirm the tell-tale activates.

extra.text: Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on all categories of vehicles, including M1 vehicles.
extra.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle installation and confirm that S1 or S2 category stop lamps are fitted.

extra.text: For S1 or S2 categories devices (stop lamps), the position in length shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installed stop lamp; pass if it is located at the rear of the vehicle.

extra.text: For stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to no less than 20° under the H plane.
extra.test_case: Measure mounting height; if below 750 mm, verify inward visibility of at least 20° under the H plane.

extra.text: For S1 or S2 categories stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to no less than 5°.
extra.test_case: Measure mounting height; if below 750 mm, verify downward visibility of at least 5°.

extra.text: The stop lamps shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if stop lamp reference axis points rearwards.

extra.text: For the stop lamps, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
extra.test_case: Simulate stop lamp failure; if required by the component regulation, verify the failure tell-tale activates.

extra.text: The presence of rear position lamps of R or R1 or R2 categories is mandatory.
extra.test_case: Inspect vehicle; pass if rear position lamps of category R, R1 or R2 are fitted.

extra.text: The rear position lamps shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if rear position lamps are at the rear of the vehicle.

extra.text: Where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to no less than 20° under the H plane.
extra.test_case: If mounting height below 750 mm, verify inward visibility of at least 20° under the H plane.

extra.text: The rear position lamps shall be oriented rearwards.
extra.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if reference axis points rearwards.

extra.text: The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is mandatory on motor vehicles.
extra.test_case: Verify the M1 vehicle is fitted with non-triangular rear retro-reflectors.

extra.text: In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
extra.test_case: Measure the mounting height of the retro-reflector above ground; pass if 250-900 mm (or ≤1,200 mm if grouped with rear lamps, ≤1,500 mm if bodywork prevents).

extra.text: In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle and verify the retro-reflector is located at the rear.

extra.text: The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installed retro-reflector and verify its reference axis faces rearwards.

extra.text: When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON.
extra.test_case: On the vehicle, activate the daytime running lamps and verify that the rear position lamps are switched ON simultaneously.

extra.text: The rear position lamps may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON only as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
extra.test_case: With DRL ON, vary the ambient light per Annex 13 and verify that the rear position lamps are OFF only above 7,000 lux and switch ON at or below it.

extra.text: On motor vehicles (M1), the emergency stop signal is mandatory and, where given by the stop lamps, shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
extra.test_case: Trigger the emergency braking logic signal on the vehicle and verify that all fitted stop lamps operate simultaneously.

extra.text: All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
extra.test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal and measure the flashing frequency and phase of all lamps; pass if in phase and within 3.0 to 5.0 Hz.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
extra.test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal with other lamps in various states and verify its operation is unaffected.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.
extra.test_case: Verify by vehicle test that the emergency stop signal activates and deactivates without manual control.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
extra.test_case: Test emergency braking below and above 50 km/h; pass if the signal activates only above 50 km/h with the emergency braking logic signal present.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.
extra.test_case: Remove the emergency braking logic signal and separately activate the hazard warning signal; pass if the emergency stop signal switches OFF in both cases.

extra.text: A separate approval is required for each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) listed in paragraph 1.
extra.test_case: Check the approval documentation covers each function (R1/R2, S1/S2, AR) with its own approval.

extra.text: When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each of these lamps satisfy the provisions set out in this Regulation or in another Regulation.
extra.test_case: Verify test reports show each function of the combination lamp (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector) complies with its applicable Regulation.

extra.text: Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of the unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
extra.test_case: Review the lamp content list; confirm no function in the housing lacks compliance with an applicable Regulation.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall be identified by the symbol R1 (steady) or R2 (variable), the stop lamp by the symbol S1 (steady) or S2 (variable), and the reversing lamp by the symbol AR, as listed in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for the correct function symbols R1/R2, S1/S2 and AR matching the approved intensity variant.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for circle with E and country number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols of all approved functions.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for '148R' followed by the series digits (e.g. 01).

extra.text: If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
extra.test_case: Inspect marking for 'D' to the right of the function symbol.

extra.text: Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
extra.test_case: If replaceable light sources are used, inspect for light source category marking.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that comply with several UN Regulations, the marking shall be visible after installation of the lamps.
extra.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed or in its installation position and confirm the single approval mark is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: Check the mark location (e.g. on the outer lens or housing part carrying the lens) so that removing any light-transmitting part also removes the mark.

extra.text: Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Verify by test report that the rear position, stop and reversing lamps meet all requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced) of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, pertinent to each lamp and to the category of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed (M1), shall be applied where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Check the R48 sections 5 and 6 requirements verifiable on the device (e.g. geometric visibility, colour) for each function during type approval testing.

extra.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review the LED wiring to identify groups that fail together and treat each as one light source in the failure assessment.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and verify the lamp automatically reverts to steady intensity within the category limits.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
extra.test_case: Attempt to fit the light source in alternative positions; pass if only the correct position is possible.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applying, and where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to that category also applying.
extra.test_case: Gauge the holder against the relevant IEC 60061 data sheet dimensions.

extra.text: All measurements, photometric and colorimetric, shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraph 4.8., with the methods of measurement given in Annex 3.
extra.test_case: Confirm the test report states measurements were performed per paragraph 4.8 conditions and Annex 3 methods.

extra.text: In the case of replaceable UN approved light sources, all measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.
extra.test_case: Verify the test report records use of R.E.5 standard light sources.

extra.text: During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
extra.test_case: Inspect the photometric set-up for masking preventing stray reflections.

extra.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
extra.test_case: Confirm intensity measurements of each function were made with the light sources continuously lit.

extra.text: The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
extra.test_case: Check that the apparent surface limits for each function in the direction of the reference axis are determined and documented.

extra.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Confirm the lamp was operated during testing per the applicant's specified operating conditions.

extra.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Confirm operating conditions during testing match the applicant's specification.

extra.text: An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
extra.test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps together and verify photometric compliance.

extra.text: If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility colorimetric and photometric requirement, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
extra.test_case: Test the specified interdependent lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component for outboard visibility, colour and photometry.

extra.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Drive the variable intensity control across its signal range and verify intensities stay within the paragraph 5 range.

extra.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously to the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure stop+position together and position alone in the ±5° V / ±10° H field and verify ratio ≥5:1.

extra.text: If one or both of the reciprocally incorporated rear position and stop lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered for the 5:1 ratio are those obtained with all sources in operation.
extra.test_case: Confirm the ratio measurement was done with all light sources operating.

extra.text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
extra.test_case: Verify luminous intensity testing follows the Annex 8 procedure.

extra.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
extra.test_case: Confirm colour measurements were made with the lamp's own non-replaceable LEDs.

extra.text: To check the colorimetric characteristics, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
extra.test_case: Confirm colorimetric testing uses the paragraph 4.8 operating and measurement conditions.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd on the reference axis (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)), as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity on both samples and verify ≥4 cd.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp and 8.5∙10^0 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Scan all visible directions and verify ≤17 cd (≤8.5 cd if marked D).

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall meet Figure A3-I, as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure at Figure A3-I grid points and verify the percentage minima are met.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)), the luminous intensity shall be not less than 5∙10^-2 cd, as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure across Table A2-1 visibility angles and verify ≥0.05 cd.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 4.2∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp and 2.1∙10^1 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Verify maximum intensity ≤42 cd (≤21 cd if marked D) in all visible directions.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall meet Figure A3-I, and within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) the luminous intensity shall be not less than 5∙10^-2 cd, as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Verify Figure A3-I distribution and ≥0.05 cd across Table A2-1 angles.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Assess rear position lamp failure behaviour against paragraph 4.6.

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd and the maximum luminous intensity shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 1.30∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I and the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity on the reference axis and across Figure A3-I grid; min ≥ 60 cd, max ≤ 260 cd (≤ 130 cd if marked D).

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd and the maximum luminous intensity shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 3.65∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I and the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity under variable-intensity conditions; min ≥ 60 cd, max ≤ 730 cd (≤ 365 cd if marked D).

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S1, the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be 3∙10^-1 cd, as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity at the boundary of the Table A2-1 geometric visibility angles; each value ≥ 0.3 cd.

extra.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Simulate light source failure per paragraph 4.6 and verify the specified behaviour.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the minimum luminous intensity shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd, with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity on the reference axis and over Figure A3-V grid; minimum ≥ 80 cd.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane, 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Scan intensity in the three vertical zones; ≤ 300 cd at/above H, ≤ 600 cd down to 5°D, ≤ 8000 cd below 5°D.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below, as given in Table A2-1 (angles shown for lamps mounted on the right side of the vehicle).
extra.test_case: Check the lamp in its mounting position: the light-emitting surface is visible throughout 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally and 15° above / 15° below vertically.

extra.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility below the H-plane may be reduced to 20° inboard / 80° outboard.
extra.test_case: Confirm the H-plane height is below 750 mm and verify visibility of at least 20° inboard / 80° outboard below the H-plane.

extra.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility may be reduced to 15° above / 5° below.
extra.test_case: Confirm the H-plane height is below 750 mm and verify vertical visibility of at least 15° above / 5° below.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Compute the required minimum at each grid point as the percentage of the minimum, rounded down to three significant digits, and compare with the measured intensities.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: For a declared mounting height ≤ 750 mm, verify the photometric grid of the rear position lamp down to 5° below H only.

extra.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: For a declared mounting height ≤ 750 mm, verify the photometric grid of the stop lamp down to 5° below H only.

extra.text: The direction H = 0° and V = 0° shall correspond to the reference axis, which passes through the centre of reference and, on the vehicle, is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and oriented in the required direction of visibility.
extra.test_case: Check that the goniometric measurements of each function are referenced to the manufacturer-declared reference axis and centre of reference.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 4) in the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the rear position lamp at the Figure A3-I grid points; each value ≥ the stated percentage of the required minimum.

extra.text: The stop lamp of category S1 or S2 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 7) in the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the stop lamp at the Figure A3-I grid points; each value ≥ the stated percentage of the required minimum.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall meet, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the reversing lamp at the Figure A3-V points; each value ≥ the minimum in cd shown.

extra.text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time, if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
extra.test_case: Confirm each function uses LED only and that values measured per paragraph 1.2 comply; then compliance at all points in time is deemed.

extra.text: The approval number assigned to the approved retro-reflector type shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.
extra.test_case: Inspect the device and confirm the approval number is marked per paragraph 3.3.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall be identified by the symbol IA if it is an independent retro-reflector for motor vehicles, or IB if it is combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight, as given in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Verify the class symbol marked and documented matches the construction (IA independent/watertight, IB combined with non-watertight lamps).

extra.text: The size of the approval marking shall comply with the value for "a" defined in Table 1 (minimum 5 mm for Class IA and IB retro-reflectors).
extra.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimension "a"; it must be at least 5 mm.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle enclosing E and the country number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5. (IA or IB).
extra.test_case: Check the class symbol IA or IB is part of the marking.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Check the marking contains "150R" followed by the series of amendments digits.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Check whether rotation is ambiguous; if so, verify "TOP" is horizontal on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Check on the installed lamp that the single approval mark is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of these lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Inspect construction: verify the mark is on a part (e.g. outer lens) such that no light-transmitting part can be removed without removing the mark.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflector, where their verification at the moment of type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Review the R48 general and individual specifications relevant to rear retro-reflectors on M1 vehicles and confirm the device meets those verifiable at type approval.

extra.text: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples of the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and at least one hour after this test examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 6 Part 1 heat test on ten samples and, after at least one hour, check colour and RI at 20'/0°; values within limits.

extra.text: The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values after the heat resistance test shall then be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
extra.test_case: Perform full photometric test per 5.1.4 on min and max samples; all points meet Table 3.

extra.text: The first group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
extra.test_case: Perform the water penetration test and then the fuel and lubricant resistance tests on two samples; samples pass.

extra.text: The second group of two retro-reflector samples shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
extra.test_case: Perform the corrosion test (if applicable) and the rear-face abrasion test on two samples; samples pass.

extra.text: The third group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 4 Part 3 stability test on two samples; samples pass.

extra.text: The fourth group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 6 Part 6 weathering test on two samples; samples pass.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Measure the colour of each post-test sample; within R48 night-time red limits.

extra.text: Where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Confirm the declared mounting height; if < 750 mm, verify the downward RI points only to 5° and check that they meet Table 3.

extra.text: The testing of the colour of the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
extra.test_case: Perform the night-time colour measurement using the 4.2.1 set-up.

extra.text: The retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB shall be tested in the chronological order of tests given in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Review the test report and confirm that samples a to j were tested in the sequence of Table 4.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C), followed by a visual inspection for distortion.
extra.test_case: Expose the samples for 48 h at 65 ± 2 °C and inspect them; pass if no distortion is visible.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, all samples (a to j) shall undergo a visual inspection of the general specifications and a visual inspection of shapes and dimensions according to Annex 5.
extra.test_case: Visually inspect all ten samples against paragraph 4 and Annex 5; pass if no non-conformity is found.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, colorimetry shall be checked according to paragraph 4.2. by visual inspection, with trichromatic coordinates measured in case of doubt, after each conditioning stage in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Inspect the colour visually and measure the trichromatic coordinates if in doubt; pass if they are within the red limits.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, photometry according to Part 1 of Annex 4, limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, shall be performed on the samples after each conditioning stage in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure the CIL at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° after each stage; pass if the values meet the required minimum.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, complete photometry according to Part 1 of Annex 4 shall be performed on two samples.
extra.test_case: Perform the full photometric measurement on two samples; pass if all values are met.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the water test of Part 3 of Annex 6 (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position), followed by a visual inspection.
extra.test_case: Immerse the samples 10 min upright and 10 min inverted, then inspect; pass if no water has penetrated.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the motor fuels test of Part 1 of Annex 7 (5 min), followed by a visual inspection.
extra.test_case: Expose the samples to the test fuel for 5 min and inspect them; pass if no visible degradation is found.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, 2 hours interval, 24 hours), followed by a visual inspection.
extra.test_case: Run the salt-spray cycle of 24 h, 2 h interval and 24 h, then inspect; pass if no detrimental corrosion is visible.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the stability in time test of Part 3 of Annex 4, followed by colorimetry (visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: After the stability test, check colour and the CIL at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if both are within limits.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6, followed by colorimetry (visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: After weathering, check colour and the CIL at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if both are within limits.

extra.text: When the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device.
extra.test_case: During RI measurement at β1 = β2 = 0°, turn the device slightly and check for any mirror effect.

extra.text: If any mirror effect is produced when measuring the RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, a reading of the retro-reflective device shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Where a mirror effect is found, take the RI reading at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and verify it meets the specified value.

extra.text: When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the value of ε of minimum RI; if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference only ±5° from that position.
extra.test_case: Measure RI at all other angles with the device at the minimum-RI ε position (±5° allowed) and verify compliance.

extra.text: If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI of the retro-reflective device exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
extra.test_case: Check RI at β = 0°, ε = 0°; if ≥150 % of specified value, perform all measurements at ε = 0°.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Verify the test lab used CIE Standard Illuminant A for retro-reflection measurement.

extra.text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
extra.test_case: Expose the retro-reflector to 65 °C ± 2 °C dry atmosphere for 48 h, then cool 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C, and proceed to inspection.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
extra.test_case: Immerse the stripped retro-reflector (lamp) for 10 min in 50 °C ± 5 °C water with the illuminating surface top 20 mm below the water surface.

extra.text: The water penetration test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
extra.test_case: Repeat the 10 min immersion at 50 °C with the device inverted and rear face under about 20 mm of water.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
extra.test_case: Immediately after the 50 °C immersions, immerse the device under the same conditions in 25 °C ± 5 °C water.

extra.text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, in the case of retro-reflectors, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
extra.test_case: After shaking off excess water, measure RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and check it meets the applicable requirements.

extra.text: For retro-reflective devices of Class IB, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied as an alternative test procedure of resistance to water penetration.
extra.test_case: Check the test report confirms that both the moisture test and the dust test were performed when the alternative procedure was requested.

extra.text: For the alternative moisture test, a sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to a water spray.
extra.test_case: Check the test report records the initial RI of the fixture-mounted sample before the water spray.

extra.text: During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open.
extra.test_case: Inspect the test sample to confirm that no drain hole or opening was sealed during the water spray test.

extra.text: During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
extra.test_case: Check the test record shows a platform rotation rate within 3.5 to 4.5 min-1.

extra.text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated during the water spray test at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate) and 55 min OFF.
extra.test_case: Check the test log shows the rear position, stop and reversing lamps operated at design voltage on a 5 min ON / 55 min OFF cycle.

extra.text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
extra.test_case: Check the test log shows 12 complete 5/55 min cycles over 12 hours.

extra.text: After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
extra.test_case: Check the test log records a 1 hour drain period with the cabinet door closed.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the device, or be capable of being formed by tapping or tilting the device.
extra.test_case: Tap and tilt the device after the drain period; pass if no standing pool of water is present or forms.

extra.text: After the moisture test, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after the exterior of the device has been dried with a dry cotton cloth.
extra.test_case: Dry the exterior with a cotton cloth, measure the RI per Annex 4 Part 1 and record it against the initial value.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation.
extra.test_case: Visually inspect the device interior after the drain period and record any moisture accumulation.

extra.text: For the dust exposure test, a sample device mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust.
extra.test_case: Check the test report records the initial RI of the fixture-mounted sample before dust exposure.

extra.text: Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Clean and dry the exterior, measure the RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and compare it with the initial value against the applicable criterion.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
extra.test_case: Expose the lamp with integrated retro-reflector, stripped of removable parts, to saline mist for 2 x 24 h with a 2 h drying interval and record the test log.

extra.text: After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
extra.test_case: After 48 h recovery measure the retro-reflection value at β2 = 5°, α = 20' and compare with the Table 9 minimum and Table 10 maximum.

extra.text: Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the test record shows the surface was cleaned of salt deposits before the photometric measurement.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB with an accessible mirror-backed rear face, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.
extra.test_case: Verify that the test record shows the rear face was brushed with a hard nylon brush.

extra.text: After having brushed the rear face of a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, then removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
extra.test_case: Apply a cotton cloth soaked in the Annex 7 Part 1 mixture to the rear face for 1 min, then remove it and let the device dry; check the test record.

extra.text: For mirror-backed retro-reflective devices with an accessible rear face, the RI shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
extra.test_case: Cover the whole rear face with Indian ink, measure the RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and compare it with the required values.

extra.text: For the resistance to fuels test, a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied to the retro-reflective device.
extra.test_case: Check the test report confirms that a 70/30 vol.% n-heptane/toluol mixture was used on the retro-reflector.

extra.text: After about five minutes following the fuel wipe, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
extra.test_case: Inspect the surface visually about 5 min after the wipe; pass if there is no apparent surface change other than slight surface cracks.

extra.text: For the resistance to fuels test of a retro-reflective device, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
extra.test_case: Lightly wipe the retro-reflector outer and illuminating surface with a cotton cloth soaked in the n-heptane/toluol mixture, as recorded in the test report.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after the lubricating oil resistance test, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Measure the CIL/RI after cleaning per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and verify it meets the specified limits of that paragraph.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.
extra.test_case: Wipe the outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflector lightly with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and record the procedure.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after about 5 minutes following the application of the detergent lubricating oil, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
extra.test_case: After about 5 minutes of oil exposure, clean the surface and confirm by inspection that no oil residue remains before measurement.

extra.text: The approval number of the retro-reflective device must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark on the retro-reflector and confirm the approval number is adjacent to the circle surrounding the letter E.

extra.text: The digits constituting the approval number of the retro-reflective device must face the same way as the "E".
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark and confirm the approval number digits are oriented the same way as the letter E.

extra.text: The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark and confirm the class symbol (e.g. IA or IB) is placed diametrically opposite the approval number relative to the circle.
